2010_008_081710regmtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education met in regular session on Tuesday, August 17, 2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, with Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D. and Assistant Superintendent for Business Services Mark S. Rajter. The packet is dominated by the June and July 2010 Treasurer's Reports — full Pentamation check registers, ACH debit and wire-transfer schedules, and fund-level budget-to-actual statements showing a June 30, 2010 General Fund balance of $12,510,272 — together with action items extending the diesel fuel contract with RKA Petroleum Company in an amount not to exceed $330,000.00 and awarding infrared classroom microphones to VSC, Inc. for $74,641.00.
2010_008_081710regmtg.page:
**Meeting**
Troy School District (City of Troy, County of Oakland, Michigan) Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, August 17, 2010, 7:00 p.m., Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Board members named: Underwood (President), Miletti (Vice President), Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Philippart, Pochodylo.

**Recognition**
Mr. Jolly read biographies of 27 spring-sport All-State athletes, coached by Lori Uchwal (synchronized swim), Matt Richardson (girls track), Elizabeth Waters (girls lacrosse), Tom Calnen (softball), Brian Zawislak (girls soccer), Lucas Ortego (water polo) and Eric Prowse (boys track). Most attend Troy High School; Amanda Sliney attends Athens High School and Kaylin Youn the International Academy.

**Consent agenda (item 5)**
Minutes of the July 13, 2010 meeting (resolutions 10-069 through 10-080, each carried 6-0 with Miletti absent), the Treasurer's Reports for June and July 2010, and the diesel fuel bid award. The July resolutions awarded elementary science kits to Delta Education ($138,280.00), playground surface materials to Rolar Property Services ($74,340.00) and radio frequency microphones to Videotape Products, Inc. ($24,623.05), all from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund; enrolled six secondary schools in the MHSAA for August 1, 2010 through July 31, 2011; and named Mark S. Rajter Board Treasurer for July through December 2010.

**Fund balances**
June YTD, FY2010: General Fund revenue of $135,916,301 against expenditures of $137,649,866, excess revenue over (under) expenditures of (2,474,277), and a balance moving from $14,984,549 on July 1, 2009 to $12,510,272 at June 30, 2010. Debt Service ended at $946,534, Capital Projects at $8,441,765, consolidated Special Revenue at $7,639,053, Food Service at $925,233, Adult and Community Education at $1,103,654, Durant unchanged at $5,610,166, and Internal Service at $33,531.
July YTD, FY2011 (one month of actuals against original budget): General Fund balance $18,120,438 on July 1, 2010 projected to $16,635,541 at June 30, 2011. A footnote states the budget-resolution Special Revenue balance of $7,639,053 "included $5,610,166 Durant fund balance that beginning 2010-2011 is part of General Fund," leaving $2,028,887.

**Action items**
5.C — Diesel fuel contract extended to RKA Petroleum Company, not to exceed $330,000.00 from the 2010-11 General Fund; Bid Award #9147; estimated usage 160,000 gallons; total 2009/10 diesel cost was $268,119.
6.A-6.C — Probationary 2010-2011 contracts for Kathy Cappuso, Angela DeClerck, Courtney Fix, James Kurecka, Eileen Rabourn, Nanette Renkiewicz and Jennifer Royston; resignation of Tim McAvoy, Director of Community Relations, effective August 9, 2010; appointment of Kerry Birmingham as Director of Community & Media Relations effective August 23, 2010 on a two-year probationary contract.
7.A — Schools of Choice under Section 105c for 2011-2012: ten non-resident 10th grade students and an unlimited number of 9th graders at the International Academy East.
8.A / 8.B — Infrared wireless microphones to VSC, Inc., $74,641.00, from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund (Bid #9687, opened August 3, 2010); permanent sidewalk easement at Wattles Elementary School from Satyendra N. Basu and Indira Basu, 553 Colebrook, parcel 88-20-22-252-036, for $1.00.
10.A-11.A — 2010/11 board committee assignments; cancelation of the September 23-24, 2010 fall retreat; special workshop September 28, 2010 at 6:00 p.m.; closed session on negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c).

**Identity and meeting.** Troy School District, a K-12 local district in the City of Troy, County of Oakland, Michigan, at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (248.823.4000), held a Board of Education regular meeting on Tuesday, August 17, 2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Administration Building; meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). The agenda covered athlete recognition, a consent agenda, personnel, Schools of Choice, infrared classroom microphones, a Wattles sidewalk easement, board business, and a closed session on negotiations.

**Recognition.** Twenty-seven 2010 spring All-State athletes, with biographies read by Mr. Jolly: Merna Abdou, Francesca Adamski, Jessica Benton, Skylar Darish, Katie Dunn, Sara Dykowski, Emily Dzik, Samantha Johnson, Vivien Lee, Sophie Li, Jennifer Liu, Lindsey Miller, Michelle Moriset, Emily Muma, Monique Nguyen, Emily Raymond, Amanda Sliney (Athens High School), Kristen Soreide, Victoria Troccoli, Jordan Wheatley, Madeline Wideman, Annie Xiao, James Yau, Kaylin Youn (International Academy), Anna Young, Emily Young and Carlie Zitkus.

**July 13, 2010 minutes (item 5.A).** President Underwood called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Philippart and Pochodylo present and Vice President Miletti absent; Superintendent Fowler and administrators Bryan, Keeling, Machesky, McAvoy, Rajter, Stromayer and Witt attended, and Nancy L. Philippart signed as Secretary. Resolutions 10-069 through 10-080 all carried Yes 6 / No 0 / Absent Miletti: a consent agenda with a copy paper bid award; MHSAA membership for six secondary schools from August 1, 2010 through July 31, 2011; Schools of Choice under Section 105c for 2010-2011 at the International Academy East; elementary science kits to Delta Education for $138,280.00; playground surface materials to Rolar Property Services for $74,340.00; radio frequency microphones to Videotape Products, Inc. for $24,623.05 (all from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund); Mark S. Rajter as Director and Patricia Orczykowski as Alternate Director to the MAISL Joint Risk Management Trust; Mark S. Rajter as Board Treasurer for July through December 2010; a fund depositories and investment resolution; intent to continue summer tax collections for 2011-2012; and a closed session on negotiations entered at 7:40 p.m., reconvened at 9:07 p.m., adjourning at 9:08 p.m. Shelly Carrier, Executive Secretary to the Superintendent, retired effective July 31, 2010 after 24 years; Dr. Fowler distributed the Budget Salary/Compensation Transparency Report required by the amended State School Aid Act within 30 days of budget adoption, posted July 15, 2010; over thirty bond projects were in progress; and Senator Papageorge's School Aid Bill language restoring 50% of 20j funding, contingent on the Tax Amnesty Act, was vetoed by the governor.

Consolidated Special Revenue (520, 530): revenue 5,145,806 / 133,556; expenditures 5,445,677 / 40,948; excess (299,871); balance 2,028,887 to 1,729,016, with the footnote that the budget-resolution figure of $7,639,053 "included $5,610,166 Durant fund balance that beginning 2010-2011 is part of General Fund." Debt Service: revenue 18,916,092 / 614,408, expenditures 18,590,065 / 0, excess 326,027, balance 946,534 to 1,272,561. Capital Projects (404): expenditures 7,216,120 / 187,047, excess (7,156,120), balance 8,441,765 to 1,285,645. Internal Service (681): balance 33,531 unchanged.

**Item 5.C — Diesel fuel.** The Board first approved a diesel fuel contract on June 15, 2004 for the 2004-05 year; in July 2010 RKA Petroleum Company asked to extend it through June 30, 2011 on the same terms. The resolution extends it in an amount not to exceed $330,000.00 as an expenditure of the 2010-11 General Fund. An August 11, 2010 memorandum from Frank E. Lams, Supervisor, Purchasing and Budget (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083), under Bid Award #9147, gives cost per gallon per delivery/profit of $0.0045 for regular diesel versus $0.0147 for the Macomb/Oakland Fuel Consortium, estimates annual usage at 160,000 gallons, and records that "our total cost for diesel fuel in 2009/10 was $268,119." RKA's July 9, 2010 letter, signed by Executive Vice President Keith Albertie of Romulus, Michigan, says the extension runs "up to July 31, 2011" and notes certification as a BQ9000 Biodiesel Distributer under the National Biodiesel Board.

**Items 6.A-6.C — Personnel.** Probationary 2010-2011 contracts were recommended for Kathy Cappuso, 1.0 FTE ASD Teacher at Athens High School; Angela DeClerck, 1.0 Speech and Language Pathologist; Courtney Fix, 1.0 Resource Room Teacher at Boulan Park Middle School; James Kurecka, .42 FTE Math Teacher at International Academy East; Eileen Rabourn, 1.0 FTE History Teacher at International Academy Central; Nanette Renkiewicz, 0.9 FTE School Psychologist; and Jennifer Royston, .67 FTE English/Speech Teacher, International Academy East. The Board accepted the resignation of Tim McAvoy, Director of Community Relations, hired November 27, 2000, effective August 9, 2010, and appointed Kerry Birmingham, previously a Media Relations Specialist at the Michigan Education Association, as Director of Community & Media Relations effective August 23, 2010 on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure.

**Items 7.A and 8.A.** The annual Schools of Choice resolution covers ten (10) non-resident 10th grade students and an unlimited number of 9th grade students for 2011-2012 at the International Academy East, from districts in another county whose intermediate school district is contiguous with Oakland Intermediate School District boundaries, under Section 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979 as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996. For infrared wireless microphones, 21 potential bidders were invited and nine responded, four of them "No Bid"; Scott Bryan, Director of Technology, cited FCC action prohibiting certain radio frequencies and described replacing free field voice amplification in all lower elementary (K-2) classrooms. Bid #9687 was released July 16, 2010 and opened August 3, 2010; the award to VSC, Inc. totals $74,641.00 from the 2004 Capital Projects Fund — FP-100-R classroom systems $47,190, REDCAT RC-V portable systems $25,056, IR Sensors $895 and shipping $1,500 — covering 110 FP-100-R packages, 27 REDCAT RC-V units and 5 IR sensors. Other bidders named: Thalner Electronic Labs, Sound Engineering, Troxell Communications and Business Services.

**Item 8.B — Wattles sidewalk easement.** Grantors Satyendra N. Basu and Indira Basu of 553 Colebrook, Troy, MI 48083-5110, parcel 88-20-22-252-036, grant a permanent sidewalk easement to the Troy School District for $1.00, covering the South 82.00 feet of the West 33 feet of Lot 58 of "Cloverdale Farms" (Liber 33, Page 13, Oakland County) and part of the NE 1/4 of Section 22, T2N-R11E. The easement runs with the land, carries a $20.00 recording fee at the Oakland County Register of Deeds, and is exempt from transfer tax under MCL 207.505(a) and 207.526(a); it was drafted by Kevin M. Nalu, Esq., Clark Hill PLC, Birmingham. Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler, Ph.D. is authorized to execute it.

**Items 10.A-11.A.** Board Committee Membership for 2010-2011 places Philippart on the NCA District Team, Edmunds and Hauff on Safety, Miletti on the Diversity Council, Edmunds/Pochodylo/Underwood on Curriculum, Edmunds/Hauff/Pochodylo on Policy, Fleming/Miletti/Philippart on Superintendent Evaluation, Fleming as MASB Legislative Liaison, and Miletti and Underwood on Wellness Policy. The Board also cancels the September 23-24, 2010 Fall Retreat, schedules a Special Board Workshop for Tuesday, September 28, 2010 at 6:00 p.m. at the Administrative Center, and closes with a closed session on negotiations under Public Act 267, Section 8(c).
